The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=\pi \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=\pi \operatorname{arcosh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
